why_plausible: the same physical quantity from the certified values rather than the paired rounds
the incumbent's frame: dispositions are taken as measured, so the readings need no correction
disproved_by: the retained artefacts read systematically larger on CMM-1 after the adjustment

why_plausible: the certificate is the obvious document and a length ratio is the obvious scaling
disproved_by: QP-07 section 4 states the figure does not map to a feature offset by a fixed factor, and the artefacts show it does not

why_plausible: a transcription slip when the machine that was adjusted is not the machine named first in the table
disproved_by: the calibration event names CMM-1; the artefact rounds show the change on CMM-1 only

why_plausible: confusing 'the machine reads large' with 'the part is large', a standard sign trap in gauge work
disproved_by: correcting in the wrong direction makes the corrected rate worse than the reported one, which the second machine contradicts

why_plausible: treating the offset as a standing property of the machine rather than as something the adjustment created
disproved_by: the pre-adjustment artefact round reads the certified values, so the baseline window carries no offset

why_plausible: the week-19 heat changeover is real and significant, so the whole step is credited to material
disproved_by: the artefacts and the un-adjusted machine both show most of the step is not in the parts

why_plausible: having found the gauge offset, crediting the entire step to it and stopping
disproved_by: the un-adjusted machine's own rate rose too, so part of the step is in the parts

why_plausible: wear is naturally thought of as a trend over time, so the slope is fitted on production week
disproved_by: inserts are changed weekly, so a slope on week absorbs any step at the window boundary; tool_hours identifies it within week

why_plausible: taking each operator's own before/after change as that operator's effect
disproved_by: a shift common to every operator is not separable from a shift in the material, so only contrasts are identifiable

why_plausible: reading Schedule 3 as the rate against the conformance reference rather than the rate attributable to material
disproved_by: Schedule 3 section 3.2 names the rate attributable to the supplied material

why_plausible: the incumbent's reading: the rate as currently dispositioned
disproved_by: the agreement names a rate measured against the drawing's conformance reference

why_plausible: restricting to the machine that was adjusted, as though the correction only applied there
disproved_by: the agreement's population is the affected feature, not one machine's share of it; the csv covers all parts
the report, the calibration event and the notes all place the step at the start of week 19

why_plausible: hedging: name every cause so that the right one is always included
disproved_by: each component is graded against its own value, and the sum constraint prevents inflating them all
